skill.name: agile-product-owner
skill.description: Agile product owner toolkit for creating INVEST-style user stories, acceptance criteria, story point estimates, backlog priorities, and sprint plans.
skill.summary: Create structured agile stories, backlog summaries, and sprint plans from product epics.
skill.author: davila7

content.user_title: Plan Agile Backlogs With Story Templates
content.value_statement: Product teams need consistent stories, estimates, and sprint plans. This skill turns epics into INVEST-style backlog items and capacity-based sprint plans.
actual_capabilities: Generates user stories from epics, personas, scope items, and technical requirements.
Creates acceptance criteria for validation, error handling, performance, and keyboard accessibility.
Estimates story points with simple complexity rules based on feature wording.
Assigns backlog priority from persona, feature urgency, and improvement signals.
Plans committed and stretch sprint work from backlog priority and capacity.
Prints formatted story details, sprint plans, and backlog summaries.
limitations: Uses heuristic templates and cannot replace product discovery or stakeholder validation.
Runs on sample epic data unless the script is adapted for live backlog input.
Does not integrate with Jira, Azure DevOps, or project management APIs.
Story point estimates are guidance and need review by the delivery team.

use_cases.title: Draft New Feature Backlogs
use_cases.description: Turn a product epic into consistent user stories, acceptance criteria, estimates, and priorities.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sprint Commitments
use_cases.description: Select committed and stretch work by capacity, priority, and estimated story points.

use_cases.title: Standardize Early Product Planning
use_cases.description: Create an initial backlog structure before investing in a full product management system.

prompt_templates.title: Create Starter Stories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agile-product-owner skill to create user stories for this epic: [epic]. Include personas, scope items, acceptance criteria, priority, and estimates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Sprint Capacity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agile-product-owner skill to plan a sprint with [capacity] story points. Explain committed work, stretch work, and capacity utilization.

prompt_templates.title: Review Story Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agile-product-owner skill to review these stories against INVEST criteria. Identify gaps in independence, size, testability, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Build Release Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the agile-product-owner skill to break this release theme into epics, user stories, enabler stories, dependencies, sprint candidates, and stakeholder summary notes.

output_examples.input: Epic for a user dashboard with metrics, export, sharing, and automated reports.
output_examples.output: A backlog summary with user stories, story narratives, priorities, point estimates, acceptance criteria, and INVEST checklist results.

output_examples.input: Sprint planning request with 30 points of capacity.
output_examples.output: A sprint plan showing committed stories, stretch goals, total committed points, and capacity utilization.

output_examples.input: Backlog refinement request for a complex analytics feature.
output_examples.output: A review that flags large or unclear stories and recommends smaller, testable backlog items.

best_practices: Provide clear epics, personas, and scope items before asking for story generation.
Review estimates with the engineering team before sprint commitment.
Use generated acceptance criteria as a starting point for team refinement.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated story points as final delivery commitments.
Do not skip stakeholder review for generated backlog items.
Do not use sample output as a replacement for real product context.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create user stories, acceptance criteria, estimates, priorities, sprint plans, and backlog summaries.

faq.question: Does it connect to project management tools?
faq.answer: No. The included script does not connect to Jira, Azure DevOps, Linear, or similar tools.

faq.question: Can it generate INVEST-style stories?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates stories and checks independence, negotiability, value, estimability, size, and testability.

faq.question: Can it plan a sprint?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize backlog items into committed and stretch work based on story point capacity.

faq.question: Are the estimates authoritative?
faq.answer: No. Estimates are heuristic suggestions and should be validated by the delivery team.
